newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 30.

text.p: PRAVO - Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik has asked Skoda Auto to use some of its initial production of the new Octavia model for export instead of only for domestic sales. This step is in reaction to the poor trade balance develpments.

- Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik has admitted that growth of the GDP will likely be lower than originally estimated. He has accordingly changed his 1996 estimate to 4.8 percent from a previous 5.5 percent.
- Farmers want a speedy settlement with regards to the extreme situation in the agricultural sphere, stating that the price they are asking for grain is not going to cause inflation.
- The price of tomatoes increased by a record nine crowns-- almost one-third-- during the course of last week.
- Komercni Banka has once again topped the list of the best 100 banks in Central Europe published by the british trade magazine "The Banker" in its September issue.

- Four days before Agrobanka underwent forced administration, the Czech National Bank refused to give large banks guarantees on loans for Agrobanka which were intended to help the bank overcome its momentary financial problems according to a source from the banking sector.
- Prvni Cesko-Ruska Banka intends to offer one billion crowns of loans in 1997. The bank, the first Czech and Russian joint bank began operations in August.
- The number of petrol stations in the Czech Republic has nearly doubled from 1990 to the current total of approximately 1400.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - An evaluation of the banking sector cannot be isolated from an analysis of economic reform according to a report from Central Bank governer Josef Tosovsky to be presented to the government this week.

- Prvni Cesko-Ruska Banka, a joint venture between the Czech bank IPB and Russian Bank Vozrozdenija, opened its first branch in Moscow. The main aim of the bank is to support Czech businesses in Russia.

- Ceska Rafinerska, the only Czech fuel producer, is increasing the price of diesel fuel by 300 crowns a tonne from October 1. At the same time the company intends to decrease the price of petrol by the same amount.
- During his visit to the USA, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus invited several experts in the banking sector and the capital market to Prague.
- Tatra Koprivnice is planning to produce a new type of lorry with fundamental changes to the cabin construction. The vehicle will be mainly for export.
- The Czech National Bank has assessed the current currency and economic developments in the Czech Republic as positive.
- Skoda Plzen has opened a joint venture in Katovice, Poland. The company will manufactuire cars and railway vehicles as well as heavy machinery.
